newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil wheat output to fall 20 pct in 1997 -Safras.
newsitem.headline: Brazil wheat output to fall 20 pct in 1997 -Safras.

text.p: Brazilian wheat production should reach 2.53 million tonnes, down 20 percent from 3.17 million tonnes in 1996, according to the latest estimate from independent consultants Safras e Mercado.
With around 70 percent of sowings completed, planted area is now expected to cover 1.50 million hectares, down from 1.78 million hectares in 1996.
In April, Safras forecast 1997 wheat production at 2.51 million tonnes and planted area 1.51 million hectares.
Productivity in 1997 should be 1,686 kgs per hectare against 1,811 kgs last year.
Parana, Brazil's key producing region, is expected to see output of 1.59 million tonnes, a fall of 18 percent from the 1.95 million tonnes produced in 1996, Safras said.
With planted area down at 900,000 hectares from 1.05 million hectares in 1996, average yields are seen at 1,767 kgs per hectare compared with 1,902 kgs last year.
In the next key state, Rio Grande do Sul, production is forecast at 780,000 tonnes, a drop of 22 percent from the 994,000 tonnes grown last year.
Planted area is expected to see a reduction of 11 percent to 505,000 hectares against 568,000 hectares last season.
The smaller crop should result in higher grain imports in 1997/98 (August/July), Safras said.
The company is predicting Brazil will have to bring in 5.55 million tonnes of wheat in the coming crop year against 5.30 million tonnes in 1996/97.
Closing stocks at the end of 1997/98 are expected to drop sharply to 507,400 tonnes against 692,400 tonnes forecast on July 31, 1997, Safras said.
